minutes.headline: Parks Commission raised town beach daily-pass and swim-lesson fees, and backed moving Marshall Park's address to Mass Ave.
minutes.summary: The commission voted to raise beach daily passes and swim lesson fees, leaving season passes unchanged, and voted to pursue changing Marshall Park's official address. It also heard an update on the skate park contract, a Shady Point offer of kayak access on Lake Shirley, Marshall Park funding frustrations with the town manager's office, and a pending dredging grant application.

public_comment.topic: A Lake Shirley resident asked why there was no opening public comment, then waited to take part in the Lake Shirley parcels item.
Resident said the Shady Point proposal is going in a positive direction, thanked the Shady Point representative, and held back other comments; welcomes more resident access if the lake is protected.
A property owner near the lake thanked the Shady Point representative for offering a solution at no cost to taxpayers.
Closing public comment: one person on Zoom, none in the room, no comment offered.

votes.motion: Raise beach daily passes (resident and non-resident categories) and swim lessons to the new rates, leaving season passes unchanged.
votes.outcome: passed (roll call; all voting members heard as aye)

votes.motion: Pursue an official change of Marshall Park's address from Chestnut Street to Mass Ave.
votes.outcome: passed (roll call; all voting members heard as aye)

votes.motion: Approve two sets of minutes (October and December).
votes.outcome: passed (roll call; all voting members heard as aye)

budget_items.what_was_said: The initial request sought more hours for the rec director and extra mowing money for the new landscaping contract starting July 1.

budget_items.topic: Programming line items: parks, senior center, library
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair noted the library programming line was increased while parks and the senior center were level funded, and argued the three should be more equitable.
Beach pass revenue and the town's salary budget were compared with lifeguard costs; fees offset salaries and maintenance, and the salary line has been level funded.

budget_items.topic: Town beach house repair funded by accumulated fees
budget_items.what_was_said: Last year the beach house was repaired using fees collected over several years.
Motion raised resident daily pass categories, doubled non-resident categories, and raised swim lessons per child with a family cap.

budget_items.topic: Fireworks for a possible Lake Wyman event
budget_items.what_was_said: A basic fireworks show was described as not hugely costly outside peak season, with vendors, sponsors and a carnival operator sharing costs.
A state grant, ARPA funds and a pending Land and Water Conservation Fund grant are meant to fund construction; revised cost estimate was said to be within budget.
No town meeting funding for the project is in the coming fiscal year's budget; the chair said she would gather signatures for a special town meeting if the LWCF grant is awarded.
The chair said design work was already funded by town votes before the town manager asked for a capital-needs meeting.
A grant application due the next day would fund design and dredging at the town beach and Marshall Park pond.
A member said non-resident pass sales were a place to look for more revenue.

transfers.description: Open Space Committee recommended transferring two town parcels at Lake Shirley to Parks and Recreation; later said the committee asked to transfer the properties.

decisions.decision: The chair may sign the skate park contract once Town Counsel finalizes insurance terms and test provisions; no new vote needed.

Commission will draft comments on the Shady Point offer and send them to the Select Board before its next meeting, and will pursue running the program under its own charter authority if the board does not act.
Meet March 20 to select OPM RFQ finalists and March 27 for interviews, at 7 pm.
Chair and Chris Ruth to coordinate by email on a timeline for the town beach house work.
Beach pass definitions (family, senior, individual) stay unchanged.
Colleen to lead Earth Day plans using a Google form of projects and general advertising, as last year.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to raise town beach daily-pass and swim-lesson fees, leaving season passes unchanged.
The commission voted to pursue an official change of Marshall Park's address from Chestnut Street to Mass Ave.
The commission will send comments on a Shady Point kayak-access offer on Lake Shirley to the Select Board, and will run the program under its own charter if the board does not act.
The chair may sign the skate park contract once Town Counsel finalizes insurance and testing terms, with no new vote needed.
No town funding for Marshall Park construction is in the coming fiscal year's budget; the chair said she would gather signatures for a special town meeting if a pending grant is awarded.

why_it_matters: Anyone who buys a beach daily pass or swim lessons will pay the new schedule, and the fees offset beach salaries and maintenance, so they bear on what the town budget has to cover.
Marshall Park construction depends on grants and a possible special town meeting vote, so residents may be asked to vote on funding if the pending federal grant is awarded.
watch_next: March 20 meeting to select finalists from the OPM RFQ, then interviews on March 27 at 7 pm.
The Select Board's response to the commission's comments on the Shady Point kayak-access offer.
